source_text: Ἀναλάβετε τὴν ἐπιστολὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου τοῦ ἀποστόλου. τί πρῶτον ὑμῖν ἐν ἀρχῇ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἔγραψεν ; ἐπ’ ἀληθείας πνευματικῶς ἐπέστειλεν ὑμῖν περὶ ἑαυτοῦ τε καὶ Κηφᾶ τε καὶ Ἀπολλώ, διὰ τὸ καὶ τότε προσκλίσεις ὑμᾶς πεποιῆσθαι. ἀλλ’ ἡ πρόσκλισις ἐκείνη ἥττονα ἁμαρτίαν ὑμῖν προσήνεγκεν: προσεκλίθητε γὰρ ἀποστόλοις μεμαρτυρημένοις καὶ ἀνδρὶ δεδοκιμασμένῳ παῤ αὐτοῖς. νυνὶ δὲ κατανοήσατε, τίνες ὑμᾶς διέστρεψαν καὶ τὸ σεμνὸν τῆς περιβοήτου φιλαδελφίας ὑμῶν ἐμείωσαν. αἰσχρά, ἀγαπητοί, καὶ λίαν αἰσχρά, καὶ ἀνάξια τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ ἀγωγῆς ἀκούεσθαι, τὴν βεβαιοτάτην καὶ ἀρχαίαν Κορινθίων ἐκκλησίαν δἰ ἓν ἢ δύο πρόσωπα στασιάζειν πρὸς τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους: καὶ αὕτη ἡ ἀκοὴ οὐ μόνον εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐχώρησεν, ἀλλὰ καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἑτεροκλινεῖς ὑπάρχοντας ἀφ̓ ἡμῶν, ὥστε καὶ βλασφημίας ἐπιφέρεσθαι τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου διὰ τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀφροσύνην, ἑαυτοῖς δὲ κίνδυνον ἐπεξεργάζεσθαι.
pass_a_gloss: Take the letter of the blessed Paul the apostle; what first in the beginning of the gospel he wrote to you; truly spiritually he sent to you concerning himself and Cephas and Apollos, because also then divisions among you had been made. But that division brought to you a lesser sin; for you were inclined towards apostles who had been testified to and a man who had been approved by them. Now consider, who have perverted you and have diminished the noble thing of your famous love for one another. Shameful, beloved, and very shameful, and unworthy to be heard of the conduct in Christ, the most confirmed and ancient church of the Corinthians to be in a state of rebellion against the presbyters on account of one or two persons; and this report has not only reached us, but also those who are at variance with us, so that even blasphemies are brought upon the name of the Lord because of your foolishness, and you are working out danger for yourselves.

lemmas.gloss: to be in a state of rebellion

pass_b_english: Take up the letter of the blessed apostle Paul and consider what he wrote to you at the very beginning of the gospel. He truly wrote to you under the Spirit's guidance about himself, Cephas, and Apollos, because even then you had formed factions. But that division brought you a lesser sin, since you were aligning yourselves with apostles who had been testified to and with a man approved by them. Now consider who has led you astray and diminished the noble character of your renowned brotherly love. It is shameful, beloved, utterly shameful, and unworthy of the conduct that belongs to life in Christ, that the most established and ancient church of the Corinthians should be in rebellion against its presbyters because of one or two persons. This report has reached not only us, but also those who differ from us, so that blasphemies are heaped on the Lord's name because of your folly, and you are bringing danger upon yourselves.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the complex clauses regarding the nature of the division and the resulting blasphemy. The translation of 'στασιάζειν' as 'to be in a state of rebellion' (Pass A) and 'in rebellion' (Pass B) is faithful to the sense of factionalism/sedition. The distinction between the apostles and the 'man approved by them' (referring to Timothy) is preserved. No omissions or additions were noted.
